html:
San Basilio de Palenque is a village near Cartagena in Colombia, founded by Africans who escaped slavery in the 1600s. It is known as one of the first free towns in the Americas.

Enslaved people often fled Cartagena into the swamps and hills, where they built fortified villages called palenques. One famous leader, Benkos Biohó, led a revolt around 1600. The Spanish could not defeat the palenque, and in 1713 the crown recognised the freedom of its people.

Palenque keeps its own language, Palenquero, a creole mixing Spanish and Bantu tongues, along with funeral rites, music and medicine from Africa. UNESCO listed its cultural space in 2005. It is a symbol of Afro-Colombian identity in Colombia, like the Maroons of Suriname and Palmares in Brazil.
sum: San Basilio de Palenque is a village near Cartagena in Colombia, founded by Africans who escaped slavery in the 1600s. It is known as one of the first free towns in the Americas.
